tool_input.content: Three of my six findings are closed by J1/J2/J3. …
tool_input.message:
Three of my six findings are closed by J1/J2/J3. Five remain open, including two I found in the two lanes you asked about — one of them a silent-failure regression that J3 itself introduced.

No need to apologize for the moving target; re-reading against `9ac02b6` was cheap because the two lanes you care about are exactly where I already had context.

## Closed by your fixes — confirmed, not assumed

- **My #6 (queue-position over-count) → closed by `6a06880`.** Verified properly: `ClassifyPendingDispatches` (active.go:724) is *pure* — it classifies and returns, it never clears. The stale-entry `ConsumeDispatchPending` stayed in the hook's loop (pretooluse_dispatch.go:330). That was the thing I'd have flagged if the extraction had gone the other way: `ethos mission dispatch` deleting another mission's pending entry as a side effect of composing an advisory string, unlocked, on a write path. It doesn't. `DispatchBoundMessage` filters to `PendingEntryOpen` before computing the index and uses `live[:i]`, so the count and the match agree by construction.
- **My #1 (hardcoded three-file list) → closed by `60ca102`.** `scanTreeForAbortedWriteSites` walks `internal/` and `cmd/`.
- **My #2 (write-position shapes) → mostly closed by `60ca102`.** `KeyValueExpr` and `ValueSpec` added. See residual below.

## Still open

### A. The drift guard's rationale is still false, and so is the CHANGELOG — confidence 93
`internal/mission/aborted_writer_drift_test.go:16-18`, `CHANGELOG.md:108-110`

J2 rewrote the *detection*. It did not touch the *claim*. Line 16-18 still reads: "`DelegationVerdictAborted` is written by exactly three call sites, all of which fire BEFORE a worker process starts."

The test's own `wantSites` at line 66 lists `internal/mission/store.go:Close`. That site is store.go:1078 — `Store.Close` maps `VerdictEscalate` to `DelegationVerdictAborted`, and `closeDelegationSkeletons` (store.go:1225) applies it to every delegation still at `verdict: open`, i.e. spawns that were admitted and whose workers ran. It does not fire before a worker starts. The test contradicts its own doc comment three lines apart.

`CHANGELOG.md:108-110` states it more strongly: "written only by the `max_delegation_depth` refusal or the content-hash-gate refusal, both of which fire before the spawn happens." There is a third writer, and the guard the same branch added enumerates it.

The correct argument already exists and is well-written — `countBlockingDelegations`'s comment at store.go:1845-1856 explains that the Close sweep is unreachable from the gate because Abandon refuses unless the mission is `StatusOpen`. Lift that.

This is not pedantry about a comment. The guard's whole job is to make the next maintainer re-justify a fourth writer, and it hands them the wrong criterion. "Fires before the worker starts" would wave through a writer that stamps `aborted` on an *open* mission's delegation — the one thing that actually breaks the exclusion. The right criterion: no writer may stamp `aborted` on a delegation whose mission is still open.

### B. NEW, in the session-store lane: `Purge()` now swallows the failure J3 made meaningful — confidence 88
`internal/session/store.go:311` and `:317`

J3's reasoning is right and I agree with the design: clear before removing the roster, keep the roster as the retry token. But `Purge()` still calls it as:

```go
if s.deleteFiles(id) == nil { didPurge = true }
```

The error is discarded. On a sidecar-clear failure the session is not purged, is not in the returned `purged` slice, has no `refused` slice to land in, and **nothing is written to stderr**. The operator sees a purge that silently did nothing to that session, with no way to learn why.

This is a regression *relative to K3*: the pre-J3 advisory path at least printed one stderr line per failed sidecar. J3 made the failure consequential and simultaneously made it invisible on this path.

Both sibling callers get it right — `purgeOneTombstoned:544` logs and returns `didRefuse`, and PurgeTombstoned's unreadable-roster branch (store.go:361) logs. `Purge()` is the only swallowing caller. Fix: log the error and, ideally, give `Purge` a `refused` return like its sibling.

### C. NEW, in the session-store lane: J5 left a dangling reference in J3's doc comment — confidence 90
`internal/session/store.go:221`

`deleteFiles`'s doc comment says the sidecar clear duplicates "internal/hook's `clearSessionMissionBindings`, which still runs FIRST and is now a harmless no-op double-clear on the happy path."

`9ac02b6` (J5) deleted that function. `HandleSessionEnd` now calls only `ss.Delete`. Grep finds `clearSessionMissionBindings` in exactly two places tree-wide: this comment, and a stale comment in `internal/hook/session_test.go:108`. Nothing runs first, and there is no double-clear.

Small, but it is the same defect class the branch has been chasing all week, introduced by the commit that removed the function — and it's in the one comment a maintainer reads before touching `deleteFiles`.

### D. `Store.Abandon`'s own doc comments still state the pre-DES-076 gate — confidence 88
`internal/mission/store.go:1252-1256`, `:1335-1344`

Unchanged since my first report. K2/K5 fixed this exact sentence in `--help`, the MCP tool description, `internal/enable/guide/CLAUDE.md`, and `docs/mission-abandon.md` — four surfaces — and skipped the function itself:

- `:1252-1256`: "Any sign that work started — a delegation record (even a still-open skeleton), or a result for any round — refuses the transition… There is no override flag here either." Both halves false: `verdict: aborted` never blocks, and `--disclaim` is an override for gate 1.
- `:1335-1342`: "Any entry under delegations/ — open, closed, any verdict — … blocks Abandon UNLESS an operator has explicitly disclaimed it." Omits the automatic aborted exclusion, which is the thing this branch added.

The authoritative comment now contradicts the four surfaces you corrected. The class fix stopped one file short of the code it describes.

### E. `PurgeTombstoned` refuses on exactly the crash artifacts the CHANGELOG entry names — confidence 87
`internal/session/store.go:511-522` and `:355-359`, `CHANGELOG.md:189-199`

Unchanged by J3, which addressed clear *failures*, not the paths where `deleteFiles` is never reached.

`ethos session purge` calls `PurgeTombstoned` (`cmd/ethos/session.go:881`), which returns before `deleteFiles` when:
- the roster is unreadable and `--force` is not set (`:355-359`) — the function's own comment calls this "a crash artifact — precisely the state most likely to hold unsealed lines";
- `!force && (unsealed > 0 || probeFailed)` (`:511-522`) — a SIGKILL'd session is the canonical holder of unsealed audit lines.

So the CHANGELOG's headline scenario ("a session that ended abnormally — SIGKILL, a closed terminal, a crash") is the scenario most likely to hit the refusal and leave the sidecars exactly where they were. The gap closes for cleanly-sealed stale sessions, or under `--force`.

Compounding: `TestStore_Purge_ClearsMissionSidecars` covers `Purge()`, which no CLI command calls — the only non-test caller in the tree is `PurgeTombstoned`. The CLI-reachable path has no sidecar test and none of its refusal branches are covered.

Worth a decision from you rather than a mechanical fix: sidecars are not audit state. The tombstone guard exists to protect unsealed audit lines; mission bindings are not that. Clearing them on the refusal path is arguably correct and would make the CHANGELOG claim true. Otherwise soften the claim to name the guard.

### F. Residual on the drift guard: `ReturnStmt` is still not a write position — confidence 82, low priority
`internal/mission/aborted_writer_drift_test.go`, write-position set

J2 added `KeyValueExpr` and `ValueSpec`. `*ast.ReturnStmt` is still absent, so this is invisible:

```go
func abortVerdict() string { return DelegationVerdictAborted }
```

A caller then passes `abortVerdict()` — a `CallExpr` naming the helper, not the constant — so neither the helper nor its caller registers. Narrower than the two shapes J2 fixed (it needs an indirection), but it's one line to close and the guard is already paying for the walk.

## Additional note, not a finding

`ClassifyPendingEntry` (active.go:691) inlines `fmt.Sprintf("that mission is %s", c.Status)` while `internal/hook`'s `nonOpenReason` (pretooluse_dispatch.go:510) still produces the identical string for `staleBindingReason` and `dispatchTierB`. Two copies of one operator-facing sentence, in two packages, after a commit whose purpose was collapsing duplicated logic. Not worth a fix on its own — worth folding in if you touch either.

## Reconfirming the clean verdict on both lanes

**`052d18b` / `matchDispatchPending`, as amended by J1 — still clean.** The three-way switch is exhaustive; `PendingEntryOpen` requires both a successful `Load` and `status == open`, so no viable entry can be misclassified. FIFO survives the extraction: `ReadDispatchPending` sorts oldest-first with the `MissionID` tiebreak (active.go:642), `ClassifyPendingDispatches` preserves that order, candidates are appended in order, `candidates[0]` is returned — the skip loop cannot reach past an earlier viable entry. A lone unresolvable entry falls through to Tier A/B. Only provably-non-open entries are cleared, and only inside the hook loop, under the dispatch-pending lock.

**`6c601df` as amended by J3 — the mechanics are clean; B, C, and E are the open items.** Clear-before-remove is the right order. All three `Clear*` primitives are no-op-on-missing (active.go:414, :679, :779), so the happy path stays silent and `errors.Join` returns nil. `clearMissionSidecars` is strictly per-session-ID — no path by which purging session A touches session B. `s.root` is the global root at the only non-test `session.NewStore` call site (`cmd/ethos/identity.go:161`). `purgeOneTombstoned` reads `SessionBoundMissions` (store.go:456) before `deleteFiles` (store.go:544), so the read still sees the sidecars. `Delete` correctly skips the lock-file removal when `deleteFiles` errors, so the retry token survives intact. All `Delete` callers are genuine teardown paths.

Suggested order: A (the guard is actively teaching the wrong invariant), B (silent failure on a path J3 just made consequential), then C, D, E, F.
